summary: Bremelanotide is a peptide in the melanocortin agonists class (MC4 receptor agonist). Europe PMC indexes 127 publications naming it or a listed alias in a title or abstract, including 14 randomized controlled trials and 9 clinical trials of any design, as of 2026-09-14. The strongest evidence tier in that literature is an approved medicine with a regulator-reviewed label. This page reports what those studies state, sentence by sentence, with each statement tied to its source and labeled by the kind of evidence it is. It does not recommend use, and it does not translate study doses into anything personal.

seo.title: Bremelanotide: what the research shows
seo.description: Bremelanotide research, cited: 127 indexed publications, 14 randomized trials. Evidence tier on every claim; nothing is advice.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,202, 2022: administration by subcutaneous route reported. Patients self-administered bremelanotide 1.75 mg or placebo subcutaneously using an autoinjector, as needed, before sexual activity for 24 weeks.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: Patients self-administered bremelanotide 1.75 mg or placebo subcutaneously using an autoinjector, as needed, before sexual activity for 24 weeks.
routes_studied.plain: In the RECONNECT phase 3 studies, women injected bremelanotide 1.75 mg or placebo under the skin themselves with an autoinjector, as needed before sexual activity, for 24 weeks.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=267, 2019: administration by subcutaneous route reported. Two identical phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trials (RECONNECT) evaluated the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide 1.75 mg administered subcutaneously as needed in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: Two identical phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trials (RECONNECT) evaluated the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide 1.75 mg administered subcutaneously as needed in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder.
routes_studied.plain: Two identical 2019 phase 3 trials (RECONNECT, Kingsberg) gave bremelanotide 1.75 mg by injection under the skin, as needed, to premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder (persistently low sexual desire).

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2019: administration by subcutaneous route reported. Clinical implications These responder definitions were subsequently used in the bremelanotide phase 3 registration studies (RECONNECT) that evaluated the safety and efficacy of the bremelanotide 1.75 mg subcutaneous dose in premenopausal women with HSDD.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: Clinical implications These responder definitions were subsequently used in the bremelanotide phase 3 registration studies (RECONNECT) that evaluated the safety and efficacy of the bremelanotide 1.75 mg subcutaneous dose in premenopausal women with HSDD.
routes_studied.plain: A 2019 analysis of a phase 2b dose-ranging study (Althof) notes that the later phase 3 RECONNECT studies tested a 1.75 mg dose injected under the skin in premenopausal women with low sexual desire.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2017: administration by subcutaneous route reported. Bremelanotide is an on-demand, subcutaneous melanocortin-receptor agonist that binds to the melanocortin receptor 4 and is being developed for the treatment of female sexual dysfunction.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: Bremelanotide is an on-demand, subcutaneous melanocortin-receptor agonist that binds to the melanocortin receptor 4 and is being developed for the treatment of female sexual dysfunction.
routes_studied.plain: Background: a 2017 trial report (White) describes bremelanotide as an on-demand drug injected under the skin that acts on the melanocortin 4 receptor, developed for female sexual dysfunction.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2005: administration by intranasal route reported. Nineteen patients with erectile dysfunction who were responders to either Viagra or Levitra by self-report were given 25 mg sildenafil and 7.5 mg intranasal PT-141, 25 mg sildenafil and an intranasal placebo spray, and a placebo tablet and an intranasal placebo spray in a randomized cross-over design.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: Nineteen patients with erectile dysfunction who were responders to either Viagra or Levitra by self-report were given 25 mg sildenafil and 7.5 mg intranasal PT-141, 25 mg sildenafil and an intranasal placebo spray, and a placebo tablet and an intranasal placebo spray in a randomized cross-over design.
routes_studied.plain: In a 2005 crossover study (Diamond), nineteen men with erectile dysfunction received PT-141 as a 7.5 mg nasal spray with 25 mg sildenafil, sildenafil with a placebo spray, or placebo only.

routes_studied.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2004: administration by subcutaneous route reported. PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analog, was evaluated following subcutaneous administration to healthy male subjects and to patients with erectile dysfunction (ED) who report an inadequate response to Viagra.
routes_studied.source_excerpt: PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analog, was evaluated following subcutaneous administration to healthy male subjects and to patients with erectile dysfunction (ED) who report an inadequate response to Viagra.
routes_studied.plain: A 2004 study (Rosen) gave PT-141 by injection under the skin to healthy men and to men with erectile dysfunction who had responded poorly to Viagra.

interactions.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=24, 2017: This was a Phase I study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and hemodynamic and pharmacokinetic effects of bremelanotide (BMT) coadministered with ethanol to healthy male and female participants.
interactions.source_excerpt: This was a Phase I study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and hemodynamic and pharmacokinetic effects of bremelanotide (BMT) coadministered with ethanol to healthy male and female participants.
interactions.plain: A 2017 phase 1 study (Clayton) in healthy men and women tested the safety, blood pressure and heart effects, and blood levels of bremelanotide when taken with alcohol.

interactions.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2005: To evaluate the safety and pharmacodynamic effect of co-administration of subtherapeutic doses of PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analogue, and sildenafil to patients with erectile dysfunction.
interactions.source_excerpt: To evaluate the safety and pharmacodynamic effect of co-administration of subtherapeutic doses of PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analogue, and sildenafil to patients with erectile dysfunction.
interactions.plain: A 2005 study (Diamond) tested the safety and effect of combining low doses of PT-141 with sildenafil in men with erectile dysfunction.

interactions.value: Animal study, 2025: The results of this study are discussed in conjunction with similar studies in rats, with the conclusion that bremelanotide does not act on the VTA-NAc reward circuit and does not enhance the rewarding effects of sexual interactions.
interactions.source_excerpt: The results of this study are discussed in conjunction with similar studies in rats, with the conclusion that bremelanotide does not act on the VTA-NAc reward circuit and does not enhance the rewarding effects of sexual interactions.
interactions.plain: In female Syrian hamsters, a 2025 study (Borland), read alongside similar work in rats, concluded bremelanotide does not act on the brain's VTA-NAc reward circuit or increase the reward of sexual activity.

exclusion_criteria.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=267, 2019: Patients were excluded if they were pregnant or nursing; had any other female sexual dysfunction; or were diagnosed with or being treated for depression, psychosis, bipolar disorder, or substance abuse within 6 months before screening.
exclusion_criteria.source_excerpt: Patients were excluded if they were pregnant or nursing; had any other female sexual dysfunction; or were diagnosed with or being treated for depression, psychosis, bipolar disorder, or substance abuse within 6 months before screening.
exclusion_criteria.plain: The two phase 3 RECONNECT trials excluded women who were pregnant or nursing, and women diagnosed with or treated for depression, psychosis, bipolar disorder or substance abuse in the previous 6 months.

exclusion_criteria.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2017: Exclusion criteria included any unstable medical condition including any recent cardiac or cerebrovascular disorder, and uncontrolled treated or untreated hypertension, defined as a repeated observation of a SBP at least 140 mmHg or DBP at least 90 mmHg during the screening period
exclusion_criteria.source_excerpt: Exclusion criteria included any unstable medical condition including any recent cardiac or cerebrovascular disorder, and uncontrolled treated or untreated hypertension, defined as a repeated observation of a SBP at least 140 mmHg or DBP at least 90 mmHg during the screening period
exclusion_criteria.plain: A blood-pressure study of bremelanotide excluded people with a recent heart or stroke-related condition and people whose blood pressure stayed at 140/90 mmHg or higher at screening, treated or not.

exclusion_criteria.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=327, 2016: Patients were excluded for unstable or uncontrolled medical conditions; lifelong sexual dysfunction; pelvic inflammatory disease, cervical dysplasia, clinically significant cervicitis, chronic or complicated urinary tract infection or chronic dyspareunia
exclusion_criteria.source_excerpt: Patients were excluded for unstable or uncontrolled medical conditions; lifelong sexual dysfunction; pelvic inflammatory disease, cervical dysplasia, clinically significant cervicitis, chronic or complicated urinary tract infection or chronic dyspareunia
exclusion_criteria.plain: The 2016 dose-finding trial excluded women with unstable or uncontrolled medical conditions, lifelong sexual dysfunction, or recent pelvic, cervical or urinary tract disease.

adverse_events.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,247, 2022: The most common adverse events (AEs) were nausea (40.0% vs. 1.3%), flushing (20.3% vs. 1.3%), headache (11.3% vs. 1.9%), and injection site reactions (5.4 vs. 0.5), bremelanotide versus placebo groups, respectively, in the integrated double-blind portion of the phase 3 studies ( N = 1247).
adverse_events.source_excerpt: The most common adverse events (AEs) were nausea (40.0% vs. 1.3%), flushing (20.3% vs. 1.3%), headache (11.3% vs. 1.9%), and injection site reactions (5.4 vs. 0.5), bremelanotide versus placebo groups, respectively, in the integrated double-blind portion of the phase 3 studies ( N = 1247).
adverse_events.plain: Across the phase 3 studies (1247 women), the most common side effects with bremelanotide against placebo were nausea (40.0% vs 1.3%), flushing (20.3% vs 1.3%), headache (11.3% vs 1.9%) and injection site reactions (5.4% vs 0.5%).

adverse_events.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2019: Bremelanotide was safe and well tolerated and demonstrated significant improvement in efficacy vs placebo in the phase 2b trial.
adverse_events.source_excerpt: Bremelanotide was safe and well tolerated and demonstrated significant improvement in efficacy vs placebo in the phase 2b trial.
adverse_events.plain: In a 2019 analysis of a phase 2b trial (Althof), bremelanotide was described as well tolerated and gave significant improvement against placebo; the excerpt gives no side-effect rates.

adverse_events.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2005: Co-administration of PT-141 and sildenafil was safe and well-tolerated and did not result in new adverse events or adverse events that were increased in frequency or severity compared with monotherapy.
adverse_events.source_excerpt: Co-administration of PT-141 and sildenafil was safe and well-tolerated and did not result in new adverse events or adverse events that were increased in frequency or severity compared with monotherapy.
adverse_events.plain: In a 2005 study in men with erectile dysfunction (Diamond), combining PT-141 with sildenafil was well tolerated, with no new or more frequent or severe side effects than either drug alone.

adverse_events.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2004: PT-141 was safe and well tolerated in both studies.
adverse_events.source_excerpt: PT-141 was safe and well tolerated in both studies.
adverse_events.plain: In two 2004 studies of PT-141 injected under the skin (Rosen), the drug was reported as well tolerated; the excerpt gives no side-effect rates.

adverse_events.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2004: PT-141 was safely administered and well tolerated in both studies.
adverse_events.source_excerpt: PT-141 was safely administered and well tolerated in both studies.
adverse_events.plain: In two 2004 placebo-controlled studies of PT-141 nasal spray (Diamond), the drug was reported as well tolerated; the excerpt gives no side-effect rates.

adverse_events.value: Human study, humans, 2019: Women who completed the 24-week double-blind core phase of RECONNECT, composed of two parallel phase 3 trials (301 and 302) examining the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide compared with placebo in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, could enroll in the 52-week open-label extension, provided they had not experienced serious adverse events during the core phase.
adverse_events.source_excerpt: Women who completed the 24-week double-blind core phase of RECONNECT, composed of two parallel phase 3 trials (301 and 302) examining the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide compared with placebo in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, could enroll in the 52-week open-label extension, provided they had not experienced serious adverse events during the core phase.
adverse_events.plain: Women who finished the 24-week RECONNECT trials (301 and 302) without serious side effects could join a 52-week open-label extension, in which everyone knew they were taking bremelanotide.

biomarkers_monitored.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,202, 2022: This report investigates efficacy of bremelanotide versus placebo according to prespecified subgroups (age, weight, body mass index [BMI], and bioavailable testosterone) in the RECONNECT studies.
biomarkers_monitored.source_excerpt: This report investigates efficacy of bremelanotide versus placebo according to prespecified subgroups (age, weight, body mass index [BMI], and bioavailable testosterone) in the RECONNECT studies.
biomarkers_monitored.plain: This 2022 RECONNECT analysis (Simon) compared bremelanotide with placebo within prespecified subgroups by age, weight, BMI and bioavailable testosterone (the share of testosterone available to the body).

biomarkers_monitored.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,247, 2022: Although not deemed clinically important, bremelanotide should be used with caution in patients at risk of cardiovascular disease, and blood pressure should be well controlled during treatment.
biomarkers_monitored.source_excerpt: Although not deemed clinically important, bremelanotide should be used with caution in patients at risk of cardiovascular disease, and blood pressure should be well controlled during treatment.
biomarkers_monitored.plain: A 2022 safety review (Clayton) advised caution in people at risk of heart disease and well-controlled blood pressure during treatment, while judging the blood pressure effects not clinically important.

biomarkers_monitored.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2019: Althof S, Derogatis LR, Greenberg S, et al. Responder Analyses from a Phase 2b Dose-Ranging Study of Bremelanotide.
biomarkers_monitored.source_excerpt: Althof S, Derogatis LR, Greenberg S, et al. Responder Analyses from a Phase 2b Dose-Ranging Study of Bremelanotide.
biomarkers_monitored.plain: Background: the excerpt is only the citation of a 2019 phase 2b dose-ranging study of bremelanotide (Althof); it names no measurements.

biomarkers_monitored.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2017: We studied the effects of bremelanotide administration on ambulatory BP and heart rate (HR), in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and parallel-arm trial of three doses of bremelanotide (0.75, 1.25, and 1.75 mg) in 397 premenopausal women with female sexual dysfunction with normotension or controlled hypertension.
biomarkers_monitored.source_excerpt: We studied the effects of bremelanotide administration on ambulatory BP and heart rate (HR), in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and parallel-arm trial of three doses of bremelanotide (0.75, 1.25, and 1.75 mg) in 397 premenopausal women with female sexual dysfunction with normotension or controlled hypertension.
biomarkers_monitored.plain: A 2017 trial (White) tracked ambulatory (round-the-clock, out-of-clinic) blood pressure and heart rate in 397 premenopausal women with sexual dysfunction given bremelanotide 0.75, 1.25 or 1.75 mg or placebo.

biomarkers_monitored.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=24, 2017: This was a Phase I study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and hemodynamic and pharmacokinetic effects of bremelanotide (BMT) coadministered with ethanol to healthy male and female participants.
biomarkers_monitored.source_excerpt: This was a Phase I study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and hemodynamic and pharmacokinetic effects of bremelanotide (BMT) coadministered with ethanol to healthy male and female participants.
biomarkers_monitored.plain: A 2017 phase 1 study (Clayton) measured safety, blood pressure and heart rate, and blood drug levels when bremelanotide was taken with alcohol by healthy men and women.

biomarkers_monitored.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2005: Co-administration of intranasal PT-141 and a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor may constitute a treatment alternative for patients in whom higher doses of a single therapy are not effective or well tolerated.
biomarkers_monitored.source_excerpt: Co-administration of intranasal PT-141 and a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor may constitute a treatment alternative for patients in whom higher doses of a single therapy are not effective or well tolerated.
biomarkers_monitored.plain: The 2005 authors (Diamond) suggest PT-141 nasal spray combined with a PDE5 inhibitor (the drug class of sildenafil) may be an alternative when higher doses of one drug fail or cause problems.

reported_timelines.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, 2004: In both studies, an erectile response induced by PT-141 administration was statistically significant, compared to placebo, at doses greater than 7 mg, with the onset of the first erection occurring in approximately 30 min.
reported_timelines.source_excerpt: In both studies, an erectile response induced by PT-141 administration was statistically significant, compared to placebo, at doses greater than 7 mg, with the onset of the first erection occurring in approximately 30 min.
reported_timelines.plain: In two 2004 studies of PT-141 nasal spray (Diamond), erections at doses above 7 mg were significantly more frequent than with placebo, with the first erection starting after about 30 minutes.

storage.value: Animal study, 2026: The recent clinical success of macrocyclic peptides, such as bremelanotide and setmelanotide, highlights the potential of this modality as a "Goldilocks" chemical class, effectively balancing the properties of small molecules and biologics while optimizing their affinity, stability, and pharmacokinetics.
storage.source_excerpt: The recent clinical success of macrocyclic peptides, such as bremelanotide and setmelanotide, highlights the potential of this modality as a "Goldilocks" chemical class, effectively balancing the properties of small molecules and biologics while optimizing their affinity, stability, and pharmacokinetics.
storage.plain: Background: a 2026 design paper (Merlino) cites bremelanotide and setmelanotide as ring-shaped peptides with balanced stability and absorption; the excerpt reports no storage finding and no result in animals or people.

storage.value: In vitro study, 2026: Bremelanotide (BRM) is a cyclic peptide therapeutic whose intrinsic stability and degradation behavior have not been extensively investigated.
storage.source_excerpt: Bremelanotide (BRM) is a cyclic peptide therapeutic whose intrinsic stability and degradation behavior have not been extensively investigated.
storage.plain: Background: this 2026 lab chemistry study notes that bremelanotide's stability and how it breaks down had not been widely studied.

study_durations.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,202, 2022: durations stated: 52 week; 24 weeks. Food and Drug Administration for treatment of acquired generalized HSDD in premenopausal women, were established in the phase 3 RECONNECT studies, two identically designed double-blind randomized placebo-controlled studies with an optional 52-week open-label extension.
study_durations.source_excerpt: Food and Drug Administration for treatment of acquired generalized HSDD in premenopausal women, were established in the phase 3 RECONNECT studies, two identically designed double-blind randomized placebo-controlled studies with an optional 52-week open-label extension.
study_durations.plain: The phase 3 RECONNECT studies were two identical double-blind, placebo-controlled trials followed by an optional 52-week open-label extension (where everyone knew they were taking bremelanotide).

study_durations.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=267, 2019: durations stated: 24 weeks. Patients were randomized 1:1 to 24 weeks of treatment with bremelanotide or placebo.
study_durations.source_excerpt: Patients were randomized 1:1 to 24 weeks of treatment with bremelanotide or placebo.
study_durations.plain: In the 2019 RECONNECT trials, women were randomly assigned 1 to 1 to 24 weeks of bremelanotide or placebo.

study_durations.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=327, 2016: durations stated: 12 weeks. Patients randomized to receive placebo or BMT 0.75, 1.25 or 1.75 mg self-administered subcutaneously, as desired, over 12 weeks.
study_durations.source_excerpt: Patients randomized to receive placebo or BMT 0.75, 1.25 or 1.75 mg self-administered subcutaneously, as desired, over 12 weeks.
study_durations.plain: In a 2016 dose-finding trial (Clayton), premenopausal women self-injected bremelanotide 0.75, 1.25 or 1.75 mg or placebo under the skin, as desired, over 12 weeks.

study_durations.value: Human study, humans, 2019: durations stated: 52 week. During the 52-week open-label extension of RECONNECT, no new safety signals were observed, and premenopausal women treated with bremelanotide exhibited sustained improvements in hypoactive sexual desire disorder symptoms.
study_durations.source_excerpt: During the 52-week open-label extension of RECONNECT, no new safety signals were observed, and premenopausal women treated with bremelanotide exhibited sustained improvements in hypoactive sexual desire disorder symptoms.
study_durations.plain: In the 52-week open-label extension of RECONNECT (no placebo group), no new safety signals were seen and premenopausal women on bremelanotide kept their improvement in low-desire symptoms.

study_durations.value: In vitro study, humans, 2022: durations stated: 4 day. Study B was a crossover trial with six distinct treatment sequences consisting of three 4-day treatment periods, investigating once-a-day and twice-a-day exposure to bremelanotide versus placebo.
study_durations.source_excerpt: Study B was a crossover trial with six distinct treatment sequences consisting of three 4-day treatment periods, investigating once-a-day and twice-a-day exposure to bremelanotide versus placebo.
study_durations.plain: Study B, a 2022 phase 1 crossover trial in women with obesity, used three 4-day periods comparing once- and twice-daily bremelanotide with placebo.

regulatory_status.value: ChEMBL CHEMBL4297533: maximum clinical phase 4, first approval 2019. Jurisdiction-level status pending human review.

evidence_table.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,202, 2022: Among 1202 patients included in the integrated and subgroup analyses, bremelanotide achieved statistically significant improvements in measures of increased desire and decreased distress associated with low desire across all age, weight, and BMI subgroups, and all baseline bioavailable testosterone quartiles, with few exceptions.
evidence_table.source_excerpt: Among 1202 patients included in the integrated and subgroup analyses, bremelanotide achieved statistically significant improvements in measures of increased desire and decreased distress associated with low desire across all age, weight, and BMI subgroups, and all baseline bioavailable testosterone quartiles, with few exceptions.

fields.outcome: Among 1202 patients included in the integrated and subgroup analyses, bremelanotide achieved statistically significant improvements in measures of increased desire and decreased distress associated with low desire across all age, weight, and BMI subgroups, and all baseline bioavailable testosterone quartiles, with few exceptions.

evidence_table.plain: Across 1202 women in the RECONNECT phase 3 studies (Simon, 2022), bremelanotide significantly improved desire and reduced related distress in nearly all age, weight, BMI and testosterone subgroups.

evidence_table.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1,247, 2022: Small and transient but statistically significant blood pressure increases were observed during ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.
evidence_table.source_excerpt: Small and transient but statistically significant blood pressure increases were observed during ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.

fields.outcome: Small and transient but statistically significant blood pressure increases were observed during ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.

evidence_table.plain: A 2022 safety review of the phase 3 program (Clayton) found small, short-lived but statistically significant rises in blood pressure on ambulatory (round-the-clock) monitoring with bremelanotide.

faq.question: Has Bremelanotide been tested in humans?
faq.answer: Yes. Europe PMC indexes 9 clinical trials and 14 randomized controlled trials naming Bremelanotide or a listed alias in the title or abstract. The evidence table above lists the ones in this record's ledger with their design and sample size; check the study name, since an alias can refer to a different formulation of the same molecule.

faq.question: What kind of evidence exists for Bremelanotide?
faq.answer: The strongest tier is approved label: an approved medicine with a regulator-reviewed label. Every claim on this page carries its own tier, because a compound with one human trial and forty animal studies is described by both facts, not the better one.

faq.question: Is Bremelanotide an approved medicine?
faq.answer: ChEMBL records CHEMBL4297533 at maximum clinical phase 4, first approved 2019. Approval status differs by jurisdiction and is pending human review on this record.

faq.question: Which species has Bremelanotide been studied in?
faq.answer: Studies in this record's ledger report work in: Dogs, Humans, Swine. Findings in one species do not transfer to another, and weight-normalized doses in particular do not scale linearly between them.
